claims.claim: The Patients template has 22 columns: 11 demographic and provider columns (3 required), 3 identity columns, and 8 consent columns.
first_name, last_name, date_of_birth are required; date_of_birth must be a real date, YYYY-MM-DD (recommended) or MM/DD/YYYY.

checks.pattern: return 'Date must be YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY';

claims.claim: phone, address_street, address_city optional; email must look like name@domain.tld.
address_state: a 2-letter US state code; address_zip: 5 digits or ZIP+4.

checks.pattern: return 'State must be a valid 2-letter US state code (e.g. IL, TX)';

claims.claim: provider_email: if it matches an existing provider the patient is assigned; blank or unmatched → imported without a provider and listed under Needs Follow-Up.
notes: free-text note saved on the patient.
prior_ehr_system: name of the source EHR.

prior_ehr_mrn: case and leading zeros are ignored; a re-import whose chart number, first name and date of birth match reuses the patient; chart number matching with a different first name or date of birth is held for review and not imported.

Re-uploading does not create duplicates: matched rows are reused and counted under Skipped (Reused); Patients and Wounds reused rows still get their existing ID in the results file.

Insurance columns: patient_uid, insurance_provider, policy_number required; group_number, member_id, effective_date, subscriber_name, subscriber_dob, subscriber_relationship optional.
subscriber_relationship is left blank if blank; billing treats blank as Self. Imported coverage is saved as active.

claims.claim: Medications columns: patient_uid, name required; dosage, frequency, route, prescribing_physician, start_date, status optional; start_date also shown as the prescribed date.
Medication status: active, discontinued (stopped, inactive, d/c, dc), held (hold, on_hold), completed or unknown; blank means active; anything else is saved as active with a warning.
Allergies: allergy_type medication, food, environmental, latex, insect, other or nkda; blank or anything else saved as other (warning if not blank).
Allergy severity is required: mild, moderate, severe or life_threatening (life-threatening and life threatening also work); any other value is an error on the Confirm screen.

checks.pattern: /** Normalize a value to a known enum label (lowercase, spaces/dashes -> _), or null. */

claims.claim: Allergy status: active, inactive, resolved, unknown or not_applicable; blank or anything else is saved as active. allergen_name required; reaction_description optional.
Comorbidities: patient_uid and condition required; one condition per row; several rows for one patient are grouped.
Emergency Contacts: patient_uid, contact_name required; relationship, phone_number, email (name@domain.tld), is_primary optional.
is_primary accepts true/false, yes/no, 1/0, y/n; blank means no; if the patient already has a primary contact the new one is saved as not primary, with a warning.

checks.pattern: message: 'Patient already has a primary contact; saved this contact with is_primary = false',

claims.claim: Wounds: patient_uid, wound_location required; wound_type, wound_etiology, wound_status, length_cm, width_cm, depth_cm, first_seen_date, prior_treatments, diagnosis_codes, source_system, notes optional; wound_status blank means active.
Measurements are numbers with a period for decimals (3.2, not 3,2).

checks.pattern: return 'Invalid number — use a period for decimals (e.g. 2.5)';

claims.claim: Imported wounds appear on the patient's Wound Cockpit for context and are kept separate from wounds documented in Medipyxis.
Documents step uploads the files as well as the CSV; each source file is stored privately before its row is saved.

claims.claim: Documents columns: patient_uid, file_name, document_type required; document_date, wound_uid (wound_id also accepted), prior_ehr_system optional.

claims.claim: Visit History: patient_uid, service_date required; wound_uid optional (one or more, comma-separated); visit_number a number; provider_name, visit_summary optional.
Imported visits appear on the patient's timeline, separate from visits documented in Medipyxis.
